mainTopic: Believing a woman's divorce claim, who receives a betrothed נערה's גט, a minor's ability to guard a גט, and whether a minor can acquire on behalf of others.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a woman who claims she was divorced. The rule that an agent does his job is used only to be strict. רב המנונא's rule that a woman would not lie to her husband's face works only when nothing backs up her claim. Then a new משנה teaches that a betrothed נערה and her father can each receive her גט, while רבי יהודה says only the father can. The גמרא explains the argument: the רבנן say the תורה gave her an extra hand, and רבי יהודה says her hand counts for nothing while her father is alive. The משנה also says a girl who cannot guard her גט cannot be divorced, and the גמרא concludes this means she can tell her גט apart from other things. Next comes רבי אסי's two-stage rule about when a child can acquire for himself and for others. שמואל, as רב חסדא explains him, says no minor can acquire for others. רב חיננא ורדאן challenges this from the case of a Hebrew maidservant in שיתוף מבוי, and the challenge is answered because that setup is only rabbinic. The גמרא then begins to show how ורדאן could have replied, and the reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The agent rule is only used to be strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חזקה that an agent does his job is applied only to be strict, not to be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only to be strict, but not to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question it just raised: why not assume the agent delivered the גט and treat her as divorced? It answers that this assumption is only used to be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption 'an agent does his job' can make us worry that something already happened, which leads to a strict result. But we do not rely on it to permit a woman to remarry, because that would be a lenient result. So it cannot be used here to free her.

keyTerms.meaning: The assumption that an agent carries out his mission

steps.confusionAlert: The same assumption can be 'true enough' to make us strict, but not 'strong enough' to make us lenient. It is not a contradiction. It is simply a rule with limited strength.

phrases.english: This matter applies only to be strict,
phrases.notes: He means the assumption that an agent does his job, which the גמרא just suggested.

phrases.english: but to be lenient, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְחוּמְרָא, אֲבָל לְקוּלָּא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the previous part of the sugya: why not rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (strict only, not lenient)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could assume the agent delivered the גט and declare her divorced.
steps.terutzMaskana: That assumption only creates strictness. It cannot permit her to remarry.

steps.title: Why not believe the wife herself, based on רב המנונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the woman should not be believed on her own word, since רב המנונא says a woman is believed when she tells her husband 'you divorced me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us believe her herself, based on רב המנונא. For רב המנונא said: a woman who tells her husband 'You divorced me' is believed, because we assume a woman would not be so bold as to lie to her husband's face.
steps.whatsHappening: The agent rule did not work, so the גמרא tries another way to free her. It points to רב המנונא's rule that a wife is believed when she says her husband divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of רב המנונא is psychological. A woman would not dare to make up a divorce story right in front of her husband. If that is true, her own claim here should be enough, even without relying on the agent.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman does not act brazenly (lie boldly to his face)

phrases.english: But let her herself be believed,
based on רב המנונא's rule –
for רב המנונא said,
a woman who said to her husband: 'You divorced me' –
is believed,
since it is assumed that a woman does not
act brazenly in front of her husband!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the agent rule is limited, the גמרא suggests a different reason to believe her.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that she is not treated as divorced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב המנונא believes a wife who says 'you divorced me,' so her own claim should be enough here.

steps.title: When something supports her, she might lie
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא's rule applies only when nothing supports her claim. When something backs her up, she may dare to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only where there is nothing supporting her. But where something supports her, she would indeed act brazenly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רב המנונא's rule. It works only when her claim stands completely alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman would not invent a divorce out of thin air. But here there is real support for her story, since a גט was in fact sent. That support gives her the confidence to stretch the truth and say it reached her. So her word alone is not enough, and she would need to show the גט.
steps.whatToRemember: Two tools fail to free her. חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו is used only to be strict. רב המנונא's 'a woman does not lie to her husband's face' works only when nothing backs up her claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is an important limit on רב המנונא's rule. The reason we trust her is that she would not lie boldly, and that reason disappears once her lie would have some cover.

phrases.english: This matter applies only where
there is nothing that supports her,
but where something supports her –
phrases.notes: In this case the support is that a גט really was sent.

phrases.english: she would certainly act brazenly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּקָא מְסַיַּיע לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב המנונא by limiting his rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (supported claim vs. unsupported claim)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב המנונא's rule believes her in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only when nothing supports her. Here something does, so she is not believed without the גט.

steps.title: משנה: who receives a betrothed girl's גט
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a betrothed נערה and her father can each receive her גט. רבי יהודה says only the father can.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A betrothed young girl, she and her father can each receive her גט. רבי יהודה said: two hands cannot acquire as one. Rather, only her father receives her גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a girl who is engaged (ארוסה) and still a נערה, and asks who may accept her גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says either she or her father may accept the גט, and it works with whoever receives it. רבי יהודה objects that one acquisition cannot have two people holding the right at once. So he gives the right to the father alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed girl in her early teen years (between 12 and 12½)
Two hands (two people holding the same right)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two hands' does not mean two physical hands of one person. It means two separate people both having the power to receive the same גט.

phrases.english: משנה: A betrothed young girl,
she and her father can receive her גט.
רבי יהודה said:
Two hands do not acquire as one,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָבִיהָ מְקַבֵּל אֶת גִּיטָּהּ בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: rather, only her father receives her גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה, הִיא וְאָבִיהָ מְקַבְּלִין אֶת גִּיטָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: both the נערה and her father may receive her גט. רבי יהודה: only the father.

steps.title: A girl who can't guard her גט can't be divorced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a general rule: a girl who is not able to look after her גט cannot be divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any girl who is not able to guard her גט cannot be divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a broad principle about the minimum understanding a girl needs in order to receive her own divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be divorced by receiving the גט herself, the girl must be mature enough to understand that it matters and to keep it safe. If she cannot do that, her receiving it does not count as a divorce.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two parts: a debate over who receives a betrothed נערה's גט (both she and her father, or only the father), and a rule that a girl who cannot guard her גט cannot be divorced.

phrases.english: And any girl who is not able
to guard her גט,
is not able to be divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת גִּיטָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who cannot guard her גט cannot be divorced.

steps.title: What is the argument really about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the root of the disagreement between the רבנן and רבי יהודה in the משנה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What exactly are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for the reason behind the argument between the רבנן and רבי יהודה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only told us the two rulings: the רבנן say both the girl and her father can receive the גט, and רבי יהודה says only the father can. Now the גמרא wants the underlying principle that makes each side rule the way it does.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the רבנן and רבי יהודה from the משנה in step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the argument of the רבנן and רבי יהודה about who may receive a נערה's גט.

steps.title: An extra hand versus no hand at all
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that the תורה gave the נערה an extra hand besides her father's. רבי יהודה holds that while her father is alive, her own hand counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: The תורה gave her an extra hand. And רבי יהודה holds: Where her father is around, her own hand is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. Both sides agree the father can receive the גט; they argue about whether the girl herself also has the power to receive it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'hand' here means legal power to receive and acquire. The רבנן say the תורה added the girl's own hand alongside her father's, so either one works. רבי יהודה says the father's power pushes hers aside completely, so she cannot receive her גט at all while he is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra hand: an additional legal power to receive
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Where her father is present and alive

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument is not about the father's power, which everyone accepts, but about whether the girl has her own separate power at the same time.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
The Merciful One granted her an extra hand,
phrases.notes: 'Hand' means the power to receive the גט, on top of her father's power.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Where her father is around,
her own hand is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן give the girl an additional power to receive alongside her father; רבי יהודה says the father's presence cancels her power.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines a girl who can guard her גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and brings a ברייתא: a קטנה who knows how to guard her גט can be divorced, and one who does not cannot. Such a girl is one who 'guards her גט and something else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And any girl who cannot guard her גט cannot be divorced. The רבנן taught: A minor girl who knows how to guard her גט can be divorced, and one who does not know how cannot be divorced. Which minor girl counts as knowing how to guard her גט? Any girl who guards her גט and something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה from step 5 and brings a ברייתא that explains it. The ברייתא ends with an unclear definition, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds that even a קטנה, a girl under 12, can be divorced if she understands how to guard her גט. But its definition, 'guards her גט and something else,' is unclear, and the next steps try to explain it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת גִּיטָּהּ.
phrases.english: And any girl who is not able to guard her bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: This quotes the line from the משנה in step 5; the rest of that line is that she cannot be divorced.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A minor girl who knows how to guard her bill of divorce
can be divorced,
and one who does not know how to guard her bill of divorce
cannot be divorced.
And which minor girl
knows how to guard her bill of divorce?
Any girl who guards her bill of divorce and something else.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קְטַנָּה הַיּוֹדַעַת לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת גִּיטָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's second rule from step 5 and brings a ברייתא to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה who knows how to guard her גט can be divorced; this means one who 'guards her גט and something else.'

steps.title: What does 'her גט and something else' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'guards her גט and something else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the unclear last line of the ברייתא means. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'guards her גט and something else' is puzzling. Why would guarding another item prove anything about her גט? The גמרא wants to know what test the ברייתא has in mind.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the ברייתא's final line in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'guards her גט and something else.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: she guards something else in place of her גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the ברייתא means a girl who guards something else because of her גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is what it means: any girl who guards something else because of her גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his reading of the ברייתא. In his view, even a girl who lost her גט and guards some other item, thinking it is the גט, counts as knowing how to guard her גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, what matters is that she understands the גט is important and must be kept safe. Even if she mixes it up with another item, her care shows that understanding.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: This is what it means:
Any girl who guards something else
because of her bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: He means she lost the גט and now guards another item, thinking it is her גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a girl who guards another item, mistaking it for her גט.

steps.title: Such a girl is just a fool
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח objects: a girl who guards some random item in place of her גט is simply a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח challenged this: That girl is simply a fool!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר מנוח attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation. A girl who confuses her גט with something else does not show understanding. She shows the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of the test is to see whether she has enough sense to be divorced. Guarding the wrong item proves she has no real understanding, so it cannot be the sign the ברייתא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A fool, someone without proper understanding

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoach challenged this:
That girl is simply a fool!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that guarding another item in place of the גט counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mistaking another item for the גט shows a lack of understanding, which is the opposite of what the test is meant to show.

steps.title: She can tell her גט apart from other things
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, in the name of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, explains that the ברייתא means a girl who can tell the difference between her גט and other items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא: Any girl who can tell the difference between her גט and something else.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי יוחנן's reading, רב הונא בר מנוח offers a new explanation of the ברייתא. A girl counts as knowing how to guard her גט if she can tell it apart from other things and treats it as special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' means the earlier reading is dropped. The test is now discernment: she guards the גט carefully and does not give the same care to unimportant things. That shows real understanding, which answers the objection of step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and gives a new one

steps.whatToRemember: A קטנה can receive her own גט only if she understands its importance, which means she can tell it apart from other things and guards it properly. Guarding the wrong item by mistake does not count.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna bar Manoach said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁמַּבְחֶנֶת בֵּין גִּיטָּהּ לְדָבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: Any girl who can tell the difference between her bill of divorce and something else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 11 with a new answer to the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a girl who can distinguish between her גט and other items.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ability to guard one's גט means recognizing it as important and different from other items.

steps.title: Two stages of a child's ability to acquire
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי rules that a child who can tell a pebble from a nut acquires for himself only. A child who understands ownership and returns an item acquires for himself and for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רבי אסי: If you give a child a pebble and he throws it away, or a nut and he takes it, he acquires for himself but not for others. If you give him an item and he gives it back later, he acquires both for himself and for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי אסי. It describes two levels of a child's understanding and what each level allows him to acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Level one: the child knows the difference between something worthless (a pebble) and something valuable (a nut). That is enough for him to acquire for himself. Level two: the child understands that things belong to people and gives them back. Only then can he acquire on behalf of others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that the rest of this section argues about: can a minor ever acquire for someone else?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rabbi Asi said:
A pebble and he throws it away,
a nut and he takes it —
he acquires for himself, but does not acquire for others.
An item, and he returns it after a while,
he acquires both for himself and for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a minor's ability to guard her גט to the related topic of a minor's ability to acquire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child at the pebble/nut stage acquires only for himself. A child who returns items acquires for himself and for others.

steps.title: שמואל says both stages are the same
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told this to שמואל, שמואל answered: 'This and that are one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this in front of שמואל, he told me: This one and that one are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells us how שמואל reacted to רבי אסי's rule. שמואל said the two stages are really one, but he did not say how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל disagrees with drawing a line between the two stages. His words are short and unclear, so they set up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that are one (the same)

phrases.english: When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, repeating רבי אסי's rule from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: דָּא וְדָא אַחַת הִיא.
phrases.english: he said to me: This and that are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל responds to רבי אסי's two-stage rule and disagrees with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no difference between the two stages.

steps.title: What does 'this and that are one' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל meant when he said the two stages are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'this and that are one' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what שמואל's short statement means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read 'they are the same.' Both stages could acquire for others, or neither could. The גמרא needs to know which one שמואל meant.

phrases.english: What is 'this and that are one'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of שמואל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did שמואל mean that both stages acquire for others, or that neither does?

steps.title: רב חסדא: both stages acquire only for themselves
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that שמואל meant a child at either stage acquires for himself but never for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Both this child and that child acquire for themselves, but not for others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. שמואל meant that every minor, at either stage, can acquire only for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is stricter than רבי אסי. רבי אסי let the more mature child acquire for others. שמואל, as רב חסדא explains him, says no minor can do that.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, as explained by רב חסדא, no קטן can acquire on behalf of others, no matter how mature he is.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
both this one and that one —
acquires for himself, and does not acquire for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שמואל's meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither stage can acquire for others; both acquire only for themselves.

steps.title: Challenge from the alleyway-merging משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא ורדאן quotes a משנה about שיתוף מבוי. There, a man may give the residents a share in his wine through his Hebrew maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא ורדאן challenged: How do people make a שיתוף for an alleyway? A man puts down a barrel and says, 'This is for all the residents of the alleyway.' He gives them a share in it through his grown son or daughter, or through his Hebrew slave or maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא ורדאן begins a challenge to שמואל by quoting a משנה. This step only brings the source. The next step shows why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a שיתוף מבוי, someone has to acquire the food on behalf of everyone else. The משנה lists who can do this. The list includes a Hebrew maidservant, and that is the detail the challenge will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a שיתוף, a shared food merger
An alleyway that courtyards open into
Gives others ownership through a third person

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana of Vardan objected:
How do they merge an alleyway?
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה, עירובין 79b.

phrases.english: He puts down the barrel and says:
'This is for all the residents of the alleyway,'
and he gives them ownership
through his adult son or daughter,
and through his Hebrew slave or maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב חסדא's reading of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that no minor can acquire on behalf of others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a Hebrew maidservant acquire for others. The next step argues that she must be a minor.

steps.title: The maidservant must be a minor
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed. If the maidservant were an adult, she would already be free, so she must be a minor. Yet the משנה says she acquires for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of maidservant is this? If she already has two hairs (the sign of adulthood), what is she still doing with him? So she must not have two hairs yet, and the משנה still says she acquires for others!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It shows that the maidservant in the משנה must be a minor, and the משנה lets her acquire for others. That goes against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Hebrew maidservant goes free once she shows signs of adulthood. So an adult could not be his maidservant at all. The משנה must be talking about a minor, which means a minor can acquire for others, the opposite of what רב חסדא said in שמואל's name.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Two hairs, the physical sign of adulthood
What is she doing with him?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people in the משנה's list. The son and daughter are described as adults (גדולים), but the maidservant cannot be an adult, because a Hebrew maidservant is freed when she becomes an adult.

phrases.english: This maidservant, what is the case?
If she has grown two hairs,
what is she doing with him?
phrases.notes: A Hebrew maidservant goes free when she becomes an adult, so she would not still belong to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו דְּלָא אַתְיָא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that she has not grown two hairs,
and it teaches that she acquires for others?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out why the משנה quoted in Step 17 is a problem for שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation of שמואל, that no minor acquires for others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An adult Hebrew maidservant would already be free, so the maidservant in the משנה is a minor. Yet she acquires on behalf of others.

steps.title: Merging alleyways is different because it is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the maidservant fails. שיתופי מבואות is a rabbinic institution, so the רבנן could allow a minor to acquire for others there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Merging alleyways is different, because it is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חיננא ורדאן's challenge. The case of the maidservant is a special case and does not teach us the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said a minor maidservant acquires for others in שיתוף מבוי. The answer limits that case. The whole idea of שיתוף מבוי is דרבנן, so the רבנן could be lenient and let a minor acquire for others there. This says nothing about a דאורייתא acquisition, so רב חסדא's reading of שמואל still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. This introduces a reason why a case is special and cannot be used as a proof.
Merging alleyways. Residents share food together so they may carry in a shared alleyway on שבת.
Rabbinic. A rule set up by the Sages, not from the Torah itself.

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say a minor can acquire for others in general. It only says that in a rabbinic setup like שיתוף מבוי the רבנן allowed it.

phrases.english: Merging alleyways is different
since it is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: Because the Sages made this rule, they could be lenient and let a minor acquire for others here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 17-18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenge's source to a rabbinic setting (דאורייתא vs. דרבנן distinction)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The maidservant case seemed to show that a minor can acquire for others in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minor acquiring for others in שיתוף מבוי is a rabbinic leniency. The general rule that a minor cannot acquire for others stays in place.

steps.title: רב חסדא reports that ורדאן was silent
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reports that רב חיננא ורדאן had no reply to this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: ורדאן was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tells us that the one who raised the challenge did not answer back. This sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence here means ורדאן accepted the answer for the moment. The report opens the door for the גמרא to ask whether he really had nothing to say.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent. He gave no response.
A short name for רב חיננא of Vardonia, the one who challenged in step 17.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Vardan was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רב חיננא ורדאן, who brought the maidservant challenge back in step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the challenger reacted to the answer in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The challenger had no reply to the answer that שיתופי מבואות is דרבנן.

steps.title: What could ורדאן have answered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reply ורדאן could have given to the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What could he have said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what good reply ורדאן could have given. This sets up a counter-argument against step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא hints that the answer in step 19 is not airtight. There was a possible reply, and now it will be spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What could he have said? This asks for the reply someone could have given.

phrases.english: What could he have said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the report of silence by asking what reply was possible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The argument ורדאן could have used against the answer that שיתוף מבוי is only דרבנן.

steps.title: The reply begins: whatever the Sages instituted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to give ורדאן's possible reply: everything the רבנן instituted. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everything that the רבנן instituted…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer its own question. This is only the opening words, and the rest of the sentence comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reply will push back on step 19. Saying 'it is only rabbinic' may not be enough. If rabbinic rules are modeled on the law of the תורה, then the משנה's letting a minor maidservant acquire for others in שיתוף מבוי would show that a minor can acquire for others on the level of the תורה too, and the challenge to שמואל would stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages instituted. This refers to rules the רבנן set up.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here. The sentence is not finished, and its point comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: Everything that the Sages instituted —
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: (Partial) It opens a principle about how rabbinic rules relate to Torah law, which will weaken the answer in step 19.
